# Dataset card: `sim_v1` (SYNTHETIC APP / money-mule world)

**Status: fully synthetic. Never report results on it as real-world performance.** Generated by `src/presage/simulation/app_world.py` (`make data`).

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Purpose | the only dataset in this repo with APP labels plus device, session, beneficiary-age and mule-network structure |
| Size | ~390k payments, 15.3k accounts (4,000 customers, 10,000 payees, ~1,260 mule accounts), 5 banks, 120 days |
| Prevalence | ~0.24% victim payments (about 1:410); mule-flow payments labelled separately |
| Licence | generated by this repository's code (Apache-2.0); no third-party data inside |

## What is synthetic
Everything: customers, payees, devices, IPs, sessions, balances, amounts, timestamps, scam events, mule networks and drift. Parameters are in `SimConfig` and in the code comments; they are plausible assumptions, not calibrated to any bank.

## Scam typologies (8)
investment, purchase, romance, impersonation, bank impersonation, invoice redirection, CEO fraud, family/friend impersonation. Each has its own number of payments, share-of-balance range, session length, failed-beneficiary-add rate and new-beneficiary probability. The victim is the genuine, authenticated customer on their own device in most cases (12% attacker-induced new device; 8-35% remote-access sessions with unfamiliar IP).

## Mule networks (120)
Three tiers (collect -> layer -> cash-out). ~60% of tier-1 slots are recruited **genuine** customer accounts (old, normal history); 30% of deeper-tier mules are "aged" accounts; 30% of networks are low-and-slow (many small pieces, multi-day holds); holding times are a mixture (hours to days); mules receive camouflage legitimate inflow and send ordinary payments; mule networks span banks.

## Hard negatives (legitimate but risky-looking)
Large first-time transfers (house deposit / family) at 0.8% of payments, new devices, 22% of payees are recently created businesses, 4% of payees behave like processors with high fan-in/fan-out and fast pass-through, payees also send money (so "has outflow" is not a trivial mule tell).

## Drift schedule (documented ground truth)
- sudden: from day 100, large single transfers become 3-6 smaller ones (structuring) for four typologies;
- gradual: scam share-of-balance shrinks linearly by up to 45% across the horizon;
- recurring: investment/impersonation campaigns x2.2 in days 20-35 and 90-105;
- feature: fraud channel moves desktop -> mobile from day 50 to 110 (20% -> 80% mobile).

## Labels and label delay
`is_app_fraud` marks the victim payment. `report_delay_s` is the (simulated) time until the scam is reported: 1 h 10%, 1 d 35%, 3 d 30%, 7 d 18%, 30 d 7%. Experiments can instead impose fixed delays (1 h, 1 d, 3 d, 7 d, 30 d).

## Known limitations
No demographic attributes; no geography; one currency; no seasonality in legitimate behaviour; the beneficiary-side signals are strong by construction (the benchmark gets easy as soon as beneficiary history exists, so cold-start analysis matters); simulated monetary figures.
